cohort: 1751 neonates of 905 parturients with twin pregnancies who achieved vaginal delivery
finding: Vacuum extractions among twin pregnancies were associated with significantly higher rates of postpartum hemorrhage, blood transfusion, and perinatal birth trauma.
mod_finding: This study compared vaginal deliveries via vacuum extraction to spontaneous vaginal deliveries in twin pregnancies, concluding that vacuum extraction was associated with higher rates of postpartum hemorrhage and birth trauma, and these risks should be considered against those of cesarean delivery.
